spots.name: Greenmount / Rainbow Bay
spots.result:
DECISION: NO GO
QUALITY: 3/10
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

CONDITIONS
Wind: 10.7 knots from 357° (North). This is a cross-onshore to onshore wind for Greenmount/Rainbow Bay, creating noticeable chop and surface disruption.
Swell: 1.08 m from 83° (East), with a primary period of 6.05 s. This swell direction is favourable for wrapping into the bay, but the short period indicates less powerful and less organised waves.
Wave height: The total wave height is 1.54 m. This represents the overall sea state and does not directly indicate the breaking wave-face height.

ASSESSMENT
The onshore northerly wind, combined with the short swell period, will significantly compromise wave quality by creating chop and disorganisation. The favourable swell direction for the bay is overridden by these negative factors.

BOARD
High-volume board (e.g., longboard or funboard) to aid paddle power and stability in the disorganised conditions.

BEST WINDOW
A reliable time window cannot be determined from the available data.

BOTTOM LINE
Conditions do not justify a surf for a quality-focused surfer due to the significant wind chop and disorganised, short-period waves.
